verdict.rationale: Ramp ships a named in-product AI layer, "Ramp Intelligence" and Ramp agents, which autonomously take on finance tasks. These include coding expenses, drafting memos, collecting receipts, approving in-policy spend and escalating the rest, flagging fraud, and parsing contracts to auto-fill procurement requests. That shows real built-in agentic work, with guardrails such as requiring human confirmation before money moves. However, these agents run as policy-driven automations, not as an assistant the user directs task by task. The natural-language, ask-and-act experience is documented only through external assistants (ChatGPT, Claude) connected via Ramp MCP, which is not built in. Missing for 10: an in-product conversational assistant the user can hand ad-hoc tasks to, documentation of how users configure or direct the built-in agents, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the agents' behavior.
